dmm-2005-power-03a.prompt: Two functions $f$ and $g$ *commute* if $f(g(x))=g(f(x))$ for all $x$. Let $f(x)=ax+b$ with $a,b$ real, $a\ne0$. Show that if $f(x)$ commutes with a polynomial $g(x)$ of degree $n\ge2$, then $a=\pm1$.
dmm-2005-power-03a.answer: Comparing leading coefficients of $g(ax+b)=a\,g(x)+b$ gives $a^{n-1}=1$, so $a=\pm1$.
